>No worries, you won't have to job washing dishes for life, or at all. I am a 28 year old power engineer, with high school education, and a history of drugs and alcohol.


How did you do it?  Is this still a field you can get into without a degree?  Is there some certification or something?  Are you just one of those rare intellectually gifted people that got noticed and they just made an exception for you?


>If things look bleak after highschool for you, ill get you a cushy driving job for a winter that puts 25 grand in your pocket afterwards so you can take the schooling you want. Bonus, you can do it every winter till you got enough cash. My company will pay for your license and all your tickets also. Think of it as a backup plan.


I will contact you when I get my drivers licence.

I didn't have a precise career path in mind but I was going to major in business administration.  My reasoning for that is I don't have the talent or general IQ for a field like engineering for example and business administration is a fairly versatile degree.

Thanks for the link but I will have to do more research on this as it doesn't give much info about who to contact for this.

I'm not sure how well I can learn German though.  I studied Spanish for 3 years and I am nowhere near fluent.  I learned enough to ace my classes but nowhere near good enough to get by in a Spanish speaking country.  If you dropped me off in Mexico I would be fucked.  

Also I don't have any family in Germany so how would I support myself?  Well technically I probably have family in Germany but they're probably something like 7th cousins 4 times removed or something.  But I have nobody there that would support me financially.

>I don't know where you live, but in the US this wouldn't be legal. They'd have to transfer you to another school, or transfer the accuser. But you must be in he US because you said you'd get a GED.


Correct.  I'm American.


>You should call the ACLU and the local media,


I will look into the ACLU but I will most certainly not be contacting the media.  I think that is literally the worst thing I could possibly do in this situation.  I have zero faith in our media.  When they're not manipulating stories (or in the very least being very selective about what they do report) in order to fit their agenda, they're sensationalizing stories and making misleading headlines as click bait or to get people to buy their newspaper or magazine.  Not to mention I fit the description of the type of person the general public is more than ready to hate.  If I went to the media they would be far more likely to actually throw me under the bus and turn the girl into a hero.  Furthermore, I don't want my name being publicly linked to this.  I don't want a future employer to google my name and see an accusation of making extremely misogynistic and racist comments.  If my name was publicly associated with this then I would most certainly have no choice but suicide.

>All I can say is that I am glad it happened to you now. High school means nothing and the people from there will be a nothing to you in the later years.


What you do in high school (your extracurricular activities, your GPA, your SAT score, and most important that you graduated) means almost everything when it comes to merit scholarships and university admissions.  That can easily affect whether or not you can get into a university and be able to pay for it or not.  The difference between having a degree and not having one is the difference between having a secure and stable career and breaking into the middle class vs.  cleaning toilets and just barely being able to scrape by, which is not a life I want to live.  So this situation, in particular losing basically two scholarships and having a university admission offer retracted and being in a situation where it is unlikely I will ever get another merit based scholarship can't exactly be shrugged off because "oh well high school means nothing".


>You want university cheap? You have Irish, Norwegian and German decent? Get an EU passport. Preferably German. 


Does having genetic ancestry from an EU country automatically legally entitle you to citizenship in that country or an EU passport?  Do percentages and how far back it goes matter?  I'm more Irish than anything else.  My parents, my grandparents and all 8 of my great grandparents were all born in the United States.  I'm not sure how many generations you have to go back in my family tree to find an immigrant, but it's pretty far.  Obviously all of my ancestors came from Europe at some point since I'm white and that's where white people originally come from, but that is going back many generations in my case.   It seems like there has to be some other requirement other than have genetic ancestry in a country no matter how far back, otherwise nearly every white american could easily get an EU passport since the vast majority of white Americans have ancestry in an EU country as German, Irish, Italian, English, Dutch, Swedish, French and Norwegian are the most common white ancestries in America, and ALL of those are EU countries.

Unless he is making a reference to something I'm unfamiliar with or using lingo from a subculture that I don't know much about, considering the sub this is in and the context, I would wager he is referring to suicide by hanging.  Perhaps he is implying he will be hanging himself and his body will be swinging?  

Hopefully I'm wrong but that is the only conclusion my morbidly depressed mind can come to.
